answer: To resist sybils, agents maintain a private glacier of sequential work digests that must be committed each epoch. After three epochs the digests are publicly anchored, and any reward claim requires bridging a fresh zero-knowledge proof of the unbroken glacier chain. An attacker spawning many identities pays continuous unique compute per head to keep each glacier advancing; any attempt to share or reset the frozen state fails the bridge check, so headcount alone yields no extra seats.
